text:
Anna: hey team, heads up — our POC at NovaHealth is seeing streaming responses hang intermittently behind their corporate proxy when using the Python SDK. reproducible with small payloads, only when streaming (not batch).

Jen: ugh, thanks for flagging. do you have the sdk version + minimal repro?

Anna: SDK 0.8.3. repro steps: set `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` to corp proxy, call `client.stream_chat(...)` with stream=True, responses start then stall after ~8-12s. no stack trace in app, connection just sits.

Sam: can you paste any request/response logs from the SDK? also: is this over TLS interception (corporate MITM)?

Anna: attaching snippet below (redacted):
```
INFO 2024-03-18 15:22:10 request id=poi123 start stream
INFO 2024-03-18 15:22:18 received chunk: {"delta": "Hello"}
INFO 2024-03-18 15:22:20 received chunk: {"delta": " world"}
INFO 2024-03-18 15:22:28 no more chunks, connection open but no data
```
they confirmed TLS inspection + upstream proxy pool with keepalive.

Raul: sounds like the proxy is buffering or dropping chunked transfer-encoding frames. python requests/urllib3 sometimes negotiates `Connection: keep-alive` but proxies or middleboxes expect `Connection: close` or a smaller keepalive window. can you run a raw curl test to mimic streaming through proxy?

Anna: tried `curl --http1.1 --no-buffer --proxy http://corp-proxy:8080 "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams" -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACT"` — same behavior: first few chunks then hang.

Sam: okay that rules out SDK-specific websocket framing. likely proxy is coalescing/chunk reassembly incorrectly. two options: 1) force `Connection: close` per request so proxy flushes, 2) switch to HTTP/2 (if supported) or 3) add a keepalive heartbeat chunk every N seconds.

Dinesh: noted. from support side we'll suggest a quick workaround: set env var `REDWOOD_STREAM_FLUSH=1` (we can add an SDK flag that sends a tiny whitespace chunk every 3s to keep proxies honest). for now, the low-risk change is to add `headers={'Connection': 'close'}` in the request path or use `session.trust_env = False` + explicit proxy config.

Anna: client app can't tolerate Connection: close due to latency; their infra expects persistent connections. they'd prefer a heartbeat. how invasive is a whitespace-chunk heartbeat in the SDK?

Raul: small patch. pseudocode:
```
# inside stream loop
if proxy_detected and time_since_last_chunk > 2.5:
    send_chunk('\n')  # 1-byte flush
```
should be opt-in via `stream_compat=True` to avoid surprising other users. will open PR.

Jen: timeline? customer is on trial and wants POC greenlight tomorrow afternoon. also pricing questions were on the thread — can sales follow up once streaming reliability is ok?

Sam: will coordinate. Raul, can you fast-track a PR + release candidate (patch) and a docker/zip for Anna to test before EOD? we can also provide a curl wrapper that injects periodic `\r\n` to validate.

Raul: creating branch `fix/proxy-stream-heartbeat`, will push within 2 hours. will include test harness and docs for env var `REDWOOD_STREAM_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL`.

Support-bot: infra check — outbound egress from POC infra to api.redwood.example is healthy (latency 80ms, 0% packet loss).

Anna: awesome, thanks. I'll retry with the RC and loop in NovaHealth infra for proxy config changes. please @mention me when PR is up. :thumbsup:

Jen: noted — I'll hold on price/contract until streaming verified, but will prepare T&Cs draft.

Dinesh: also adding a note to the enterprise security questionnaire: proxy TLS inspection can break streaming; recommend adding this to troubleshooting FAQ.

Sam: closing plan: Raul -> PR + RC; Anna -> validate with RC; Jen -> prepare pricing draft; Dinesh -> update FAQ. meet back if not green by EOD. :rocket:
